answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of computational proof-of-work per identity to act as a resilient inlet for the network. The verifier enforces this by checking puzzle outputs against the ledger, treating every valid hash as a relic of spent energy that validates unique agent arrival. An honest node pays this cost for one identity, while an attacker attempting to thread 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles, facing a digital gale of processing exhaustion that renders farming impossible. Fraud triggers an automatic identity burn, ensuring no cheap resets.
